newsitem.title: JAPAN: TOCOM precious metals mostly up by noon on dollar.
newsitem.headline: TOCOM precious metals mostly up by noon on dollar.

text.p: Yen-based Tokyo gold futures were slightly higher by midday as the dollar's rise against the yen offset an overnight fall in New York, which saw prices slip to a new four-and-a-quarter year low, traders said.

Platinum group metals (PGM) posted strong gains by midday on short-covering, following stronger spot platinum prices, despite expectations that contracted Russian PGM shipments would arrive in Japan later this week.
Gold futures ranged from flat to six yen per gram higher.
Benchmark June was up five yen at 1,226 yen.
"Private investors built fresh longs in benchmark June gold. Except for this, there was little activity due to holidays in Hong Kong," a trading house trader said.
Spot gold was quoted at $333.85/334.35 per ounce at 0247 GMT, against $333.70/334.20 in New York on Monday.
"Bullion is expected to drift sideways today ahead of the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) on Tuesday and Wednesday," the trader said.
Local bullion prices in the Tokyo market remained low at around 50-60 U.S. cents per ounce over the world benchmark, reflecting lacklustre gold demand in Japan.

Benchmark June palladium was ended the morning session 12 yen per gram higher at 499 yen. Benchmark June platinum was 11 yen per gram higher at 1,362 yen. Benchmark June silver was down 0.5 yen per 10 grams at 174.3 yen.
